content.text: By end of year, US men 18-26 will automatically be registered for Selective Service Automated registration for Selective Service does not bring back a military draft, but rather puts more people in the pool should the government decide a draft is necessary. Posted 4/9/2026, 5:24:48 PM Updated 4/9/2026, 5:25:00 PM Related military FILE - A sign for Fort Bragg is seen, March 7, 2025, in Fort Bragg, N.C. (AP Photo/Chris Seward, File) By WRAL staff A technology update going in to effect this year takes the burden of registering with Selective Service off young men and shifts it to an automatic process. Federal law has long required that male U.S. citizens and legal immigrants register with Selective Service System. That list has been used in the past to identify people eligible to be drafted into the military. Other WRAL Top Stories Keep WatchingWRAL WeatherCenter Forecast The updated, automated registration does not bring back the draft, but rather puts more people in the pool should the government decide a draft is necessary. A law signed in December 2025 by President Trump requires "automatic registration for every male citizen of the United States” to be implemented by December 2026. The last time the country resorted to a military draft was during the Vietnam War.
